instrument_name: Illinois Minimum Wage Law 820 ILCS 105/4 and 105/4a (consolidated text, ILGA)
figure_or_rule_carried: Adult (18+) minimum wage $15 per hour on and after 2025-01-01 (no further scheduled step in the statute; no indexation); first 90 consecutive days of employment may be up to 50 cents less (not day/temporary laborers); under-18 working not more than 650 hours per calendar year $13 on and after 2025-01-01, over 650 hours = adult rate; gratuity allowance (tip credit) up to 40% of applicable minimum wage (tipped cash wage 60% = $9.00); overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 hours per workweek; exemptions in 4a(2) incl. agricultural labor, FLSA EAP employees, commissioned 7(i) employees. Source note last amendment P.A. 101-1 eff. 2019-02-19 (Sec. 4).

instrument_name: IDOL Minimum Wage Law page (Fair Labor Standards Division)
article_or_section: rate table Minimum Wage / Tipped / Youths
figure_or_rule_carried: Current rates: minimum wage $15; tipped $9; youths under 18 working less than 650 hours per calendar year $13; overtime after 40 hours/week at 1.5x; 14(c) sub-minimum licences stop being issued/recognised 2029-12-31.

instrument_name: IDOL Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act FAQ (820 ILCS 115/3, 115/5, 115/2)
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay frequency: all wages at least semi-monthly, paid no later than 13 days after the end of the pay period; FLSA executive/administrative/professional employees and commissions may be paid monthly (115/3). Final compensation (wages, earned commissions, earned bonuses, monetary equivalent of earned vacation and holidays) in full at separation if possible, no later than next regularly scheduled payday, discharge or resignation alike (115/5). No statutory severance, sick or holiday pay at separation unless promised (115/2). Act covers private employers and local government, not State/federal employees; work performed in Illinois. Payroll card: see 56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.600.

instrument_name: IDOL Vacation FAQ (56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.520)
figure_or_rule_carried: Earned vacation cannot be forfeited at separation by policy; employer must pay the monetary equivalent of all earned, unused vacation (pro rata accrual, worked examples 1-3) with final compensation. Use-it-or-lose-it during employment permitted if employee had reasonable opportunity to take the vacation and notice of the policy (300.520(e),(f)); policy change cannot forfeit time already earned (300.520(h)).

instrument_name: IDOL Form of Payment FAQ (820 ILCS 115/4; 56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.600)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer cannot require direct deposit: wages in a form readily convertible to cash without a personal bank account unless the employee volunteers for direct deposit to an institution of his/her choice; cash allowed with signed receipt; offering only payroll card or direct deposit without a check option violates the Act; itemized statement of deductions each pay period (115/10, 300.600).

instrument_name: IDOL Deductions from Pay FAQ (820 ILCS 115/9; 56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.700-300.840)
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions only when required by law, to the benefit of the employee, under a valid wage assignment or wage deduction order, or with express written consent given freely at the time of deduction (recurring deductions: agreement fixing period, same amount, voluntary withdrawal = 300.720). No deduction for shortages/damage or uniforms without such consent; no withholding pending return of equipment (300.830). Cash-advance repayment max 15% of wages per paycheck; larger balance from final pay only if agreed at time of advance. Overpayment: whole sum on first payday after the overpayment if employee agrees; otherwise agreed schedule.

instrument_name: IDOL public advisory: electronic payroll debit/credit cards (820 ILCS 115/14.5)
figure_or_rule_carried: Payroll card only with voluntary employee consent (not a condition of hire); written disclosure of all fees; full value without discount; itemized statement of hours worked, rate of pay and deductions each pay period; consent revocable at any time; an employer offering payroll card and/or direct deposit must also offer cash or check; no fees for POS, application, loading or participation; inactivity fee only after one year; two free declined transactions per month; no link to credit/overdraft/advances.

instrument_name: City of Chicago BACP / Office of Labor Standards: Minimum Wage information page (Chicago Minimum Wage Ordinance, MCC 6-105)
authority: City of Chicago, Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection
figure_or_rule_carried: Chicago minimum wage $17.05/hour from 2026-07-01 for employers with 4 or more employees; tipped workers $12.96 (employer makes up shortfall to full minimum); City contracts/concessionaires $18.50. Increases every July 1 by CPI or 2.5%, whichever is lower. Notice with first paycheck and annually with a paycheck issued within 30 days of July 1 (minimum wage, Fair Workweek, Paid Leave and Paid Sick Leave). Arithmetic check: 17.05 x 0.76 = 12.958 -> 12.96 (tipped = 76% of full rate on the 2026 figures; ordinance phase-out schedule not read).

instrument_name: Cook County Commission on Human Rights: Cook County Minimum Wage Ordinance FAQ (effective 2026-07-01)
authority: Cook County Commission on Human Rights
article_or_section: Cook County Code Sec. 42-13; MWO rules Sec. 2.04; FAQ Q1-Q10
figure_or_rule_carried: Suburban Cook County (not Chicago; municipalities with own MW or opted out excluded) from 2026-07-01: non-tipped $15.40/hour (overtime $23.10), tipped $9.25/hour (overtime $16.94 = 23.10 - 40% x 15.40); applies to employees over 18 working at least 2 hours/week in the County; not to under-18 (state $13 applies); annual July 1 adjustment to the greatest of federal, Illinois or County CPI calculation, CPI step suspended when County unemployment >= 8.5%; list of opted-out municipalities changes frequently (not published in the FAQ).

instrument_name: Form IL-W-4 Employee's and other Payee's Illinois Withholding Allowance Certificate and Instructions (R-07/23), current-year edition
figure_or_rule_carried: IL-W-4 edition R-07/23 is the one posted in the 2026 current-year withholding forms list. Line 1 = basic personal allowances (self, spouse, dependents); Line 2 = additional allowances (65 or older / legally blind, self or spouse); Line 3 = additional withholding per pay period. Exemption not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $500,000 (joint) / $250,000 (other returns). Residents of IA, KY, MI, WI and military spouses use IL-W-5-NR instead. No IL-W-4 on file = withhold on entire compensation without exemptions. A changed IL-W-4 is effective from the first payment made after the first quarterly date (Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1) at least 30 days after it is filed (employer may apply sooner).

instrument_name: Form IL-941 Illinois Withholding Income Tax Return Instructions (R-12/25)
article_or_section: When is my Form IL-941 due; payment frequency; electronic requirements; corrections
figure_or_rule_carried: IL-941 quarterly, due last day of the month after quarter end (next business day if weekend/holiday); Illinois has NO annual withholding reconciliation return. IL-941 must be filed electronically (MyTax Illinois or IDOR-approved software; >32,767 employees cannot use MyTax) unless IL-900-EW waiver. Payments (IL-501 or electronic): monthly (15th of following month) for new employers and look-back liability <= $12,000 (look-back for 2026 = 2024-07-01..2025-06-30); semi-weekly (Wednesday/Friday federal rule) if look-back > $12,000 or once $12,000 exceeded in a quarter (from the following quarter); semi-weekly payers must pay electronically. W-2/W-2c/W-2G must be submitted electronically. Over-withholding corrected in a later quarter of the same year; after W-2 issued do not refund or amend withholding.

instrument_name: IDOR Publication 131-D (R-12/25): 2026 Withholding Income Tax Payment and Return Due Dates
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 IL-941 due dates: Q1 2026-04-30, Q2 2026-07-31, Q3 2026-11-02, Q4 2027-02-01. Monthly payment due dates: Jan 2026-02-17, Feb 2026-03-16, Mar 2026-04-15, Apr 2026-05-15, May 2026-06-15, Jun 2026-07-15, Jul 2026-08-17, Aug 2026-09-15, Sep 2026-10-15, Oct 2026-11-16, Nov 2026-12-15, Dec 2027-01-15. Semi-weekly: Wednesday for Wed-Fri paydays, Friday for Sat-Tue paydays, at least three banking days (follows federal rule).

instrument_name: IDOR Publication 110 (R-10/26): Forms W-2, W-2c, W-2G and 1099 Filing and Storage Requirements
figure_or_rule_carried: W-2/W-2c/W-2G must be filed electronically with IDOR (waiver IL-900-EW; waived filers keep records 3 years). Methods: MyTax Illinois (manual entry or CSV upload; or EFW2 upload per IDR-996) or bulk transmission with ETIN following SSA EFW2 plus IDR-986 EFW2/EFW2C Specification Guide; 1099/W-2G bulk moved to IRIS format (IDR-987) from 2026-09-18, re-registration required. Due: original W-2 accepted by IDOR no later than January 31 of following year; 2026 W-2s by 2027-02-01. Federal W-2 extension applies automatically to Illinois. Household employees: Pub. 121.

instrument_name: IDOR Publication 130 (R-02/26) Who is Required to Withhold Illinois Income Tax: compensation paid in Illinois, exceptions, special categories
article_or_section: When is compensation paid in Illinois; Limited exceptions; When am I not required to withhold; Form IL-W-6
figure_or_rule_carried: Compensation paid in Illinois = service localized in IL (all in IL, or out-of-state service incidental). No IL withholding (absent voluntary agreement) on: residents of IA, KY, MI, WI (reciprocity); qualifying military spouses (VBTA 2018); nonresident with fewer than 31 days of service in IL whose compensation is not localized in IL (IL-W-6 certificate of days worked kept on file for nonresidents expected to work >30 days without time-and-attendance system); nonresident working entirely in another state; IL resident working entirely in another state where compensation is subject to that state's withholding; payments under IRC 3405/3406; STB rail/motor carrier nonresidents in more than one state; air carrier nonresidents with <=50% of compensation (flight miles) in IL; vessel crew; compensation exempt from federal withholding (e.g. certain ministers); household employees (unless federal voluntary withholding agreement exists - then IL withholding required; report on IL-1040 Line 20 or IL-941; Pub. 121). Resident working in non-reciprocal state: credit for tax paid to other state on the return. Film production / loan-out rules P.A. 104-0453 for projects from 2025-12-12 (FY 2026-16).

instrument_name: IDES Historical Rate Chart incl. rate year 2026 (UI_tax_rates_2026.pdf), direct copy
figure_or_rule_carried: Rate year 2026: wage base $14,250 (2025 $13,916; 2024 $13,590); state experience factor 102%; benefit conversion factor 138.4%; standard (ineligible / new employer) rate 3.350%; Administrative Support & Waste Management 3.450%; minimum 0.750%; maximum 7.050%; fund builder 0.550% (included in all rates); small employer rate (gross wages < $50,000) 5.4%; minimum penalty $50. Employer-only (no employee UI contribution). Same figures as US-IL-002 (wayback copy); direct copy has a different md5 but identical 2026 values.

instrument_name: IDES Quarterly Filing Requirements page (Form UI-3/40)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer's Contribution and Wage Report UI-3/40 filed and contributions paid in the month after each calendar quarter: on or before April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31; electronically (MyTax Illinois) or paper; governmental and some non-profit employers also file wage reports (may elect reimbursement).

instrument_name: IDES Monthly Wage Reporting page (Public Act 97-0689)
article_or_section: P.A. 97-0689; MyTax Monthly Wage Reporting File Upload Guide
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with a cumulative total of 25 or more employees in the prior calendar year file monthly wage reports electronically for the first and second months of each quarter (Jul, Aug, Oct, Nov, Jan, Feb, Apr, May) in addition to the quarterly UI-3/40; monthly report = employee name, SSN, total wages for the month, no contributions; MyTax Illinois CSV (plain ASCII) upload only, no manual entry; quarterly report via MyTax, FSET or FTP; penalty for non-electronic filing.

instrument_name: IDES New Hire Reporting page and New Hire Obligations page
article_or_section: New Hire Reporting Program; UI Act employer obligations
figure_or_rule_carried: Report new and rehired employees, including independent contractors, to the Illinois State Directory of New Hires (IDES) within 20 days of the employee's first day on the payroll; online or IDES New Hire Form by fax/mail (magnetic/electronic filing option); data: employee name, home address, SSN, date of hire (first day of work for pay); employer name, address, FEIN, optional address for income withholding orders. Obligations page also lists providing complete and accurate Employee Separation Information and responding to weekly-earnings verification.

instrument_name: IDOL Paid Leave for All Workers Act FAQ (820 ILCS 192; 56 Ill. Adm. Code 200)
figure_or_rule_carried: PLAWA (eff. 2024-01-01): 1 hour paid leave per 40 hours worked, up to 40 hours per 12-month period (or frontload; part-time pro rata frontload); usable after 90 days of employment, for any reason; only hours actually worked count; FLSA-exempt employees deemed to work 40 hours/week (or regular shorter week); carryover of unused accrued leave allowed (not for frontloaded leave); no payout at year-end unless mutually agreed in writing annually (200.320(d)); no payout at separation UNLESS the leave is part of a vacation or general PTO bank (then IWPCA payout applies); frontloaded leave cannot be recouped on early separation; paid at regular rate, tipped and commissioned employees at least the full local minimum wage ($15 state) or base rate if higher. Does not apply in Chicago or Cook County, which had paid leave ordinances before 2024-01-01; later local ordinances must comply with PLAWA. Exemptions include part-time college/university students employed by their school and some short-term higher-education temporaries; staffing agencies covered.

instrument_name: City of Chicago BACP: Paid Leave and Paid Sick Leave ordinance information page (MCC 6-130 / 6-105-070)
authority: City of Chicago, Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection
figure_or_rule_carried: Chicago Paid Leave and Paid Sick Leave ordinance: covered employee = works at least 80 hours for an employer in Chicago within any 120-day period; accrual from the first calendar day after employment begins; 1 hour paid leave AND 1 hour paid sick leave per 35 hours worked; notice with first paycheck and annually with a paycheck within 30 days of July 1. Annual caps, carryover and separation payout rules for paid leave by employer size are in the BACP FAQ PDF, which returned 403 (ACCESS gap).

instrument_name: Illinois HFS Child Support Services: Income Withholding for Support employer guidance (305 ILCS 5/10-16.2; 750 ILCS 28)
authority: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
article_or_section: Employer Compliance; Withholding Calculations; Multiple Orders
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers honour federal-standard Order/Notice - Income Withholding for Support from any state (Illinois form HFS 3683, cover letter HFS 3598, National Medical Support Notice HFS 3554); served by first-class/certified mail, fax/electronic, personal delivery. Employer may deduct and retain up to $5 per month fee from the employee's remaining income. Remit 1 to 7 business days after payday as instructed. Withhold up to 50% of disposable income (gross minus mandatory deductions) when the full ordered amount cannot be withheld (HFS 3683 instruction; within CCPA limits). Multiple orders, different children: allocate per Illinois law, not first-come first-served (HFS allocation calculator); same child: honour only the first order. Report termination on the 'Notification of Employment Termination or Income Status' section.

instrument_name: 735 ILCS 5/12-803 Wages subject to collection (wage deduction orders), ILGA public file repository
figure_or_rule_carried: Non-support creditor wage deduction order: amount subject to collection per work week = lesser of (1) 15% of GROSS wages, salary, commissions and bonuses for the week, or (2) disposable earnings for the week minus 45 x the greater of the federal minimum hourly wage or the Illinois minimum wage (820 ILCS 105/4) in effect when payable. Derivation 2026: 45 x $15.00 = $675.00 protected weekly floor (federal floor 45 x 7.25 = 326.25 is lower). Applies irrespective of where earned or where the employee resides. Disposable earnings = earnings after amounts required by law to be withheld. Source P.A. 94-306 eff. 2006-01-01; 95-661 eff. 2008-01-01.

instrument_name: 820 ILCS 115/5 Final compensation (IWPCA), ILGA public file repository
figure_or_rule_carried: Final compensation in full at separation if possible, no later than the next regularly scheduled payday; by mailed check if employee requests in writing. Unless a CBA provides otherwise, monetary equivalent of all earned vacation paid as part of final compensation at the final rate of pay; no contract or policy may forfeit earned vacation on separation. Source P.A. 83-199.

instrument_name: 820 ILCS 115/10 Notice of pay, records, pay stubs (IWPCA) as amended by P.A. 103-953, ILGA public file repository
figure_or_rule_carried: (a) notify at hire of rate of pay and time/place of payment, in writing where possible, acknowledged by both parties; notify changes beforehand. (b) records of names, addresses, wages paid each payday; pay stub each pay period. (c) keep a copy of each pay stub at least 3 years after payment, paper or electronic. (d) copies on request to current employees and to former employees (within 1 year of separation) within 21 calendar days, max twice per 12 months; former employee chooses physical or electronic format; if electronic stubs become inaccessible within a year of separation, offer by end of final pay period a record of the prior year's stubs and record the offer and response. (e) post paydays and IDOL notice. Section does not list pay-stub content items (content of itemized deductions in 115/10 FAQ and 56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.600). Source P.A. 103-953 eff. 2025-01-01 (fuller text than US-IL-005 wayback copy).

instrument_name: 740 ILCS 14/15 Biometric Information Privacy Act: retention, collection, disclosure, destruction, ILGA public file repository
figure_or_rule_carried: Payroll relevance: biometric time clocks. Written public retention/destruction policy (destroy when purpose satisfied or within 3 years of last interaction, whichever first); before collecting: written notice of collection, of purpose and term, and a written release; no sale/profit; disclosure only with consent, to complete a requested financial transaction, when required by law/ordinance, or under warrant/subpoena; reasonable industry standard of care. Source P.A. 95-994 eff. 2008-10-03 (Sec. 15 text; later amendments to Sec. 20 damages not read).

instrument_name: Illinois Minimum Wage Law 820 ILCS 105/3(c)-(d) coverage: employer and employee definitions and exclusions
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = anyone employing one or more persons (incl. governmental bodies). Employee includes domestic workers (Domestic Workers' Bill of Rights Act) even where the employer has fewer than 4 employees; excludes: employer with fewer than 4 employees (excluding immediate family); agricultural/aquacultural employees of employers that used no more than 500 man-days of agricultural labor in any quarter of the preceding year, immediate family, certain piece-rate hand-harvest laborers; outside salesmen; members of a religious corporation or organization; students employed by their own accredited Illinois college/university (covered by FLSA); DOT-regulated motor carrier drivers; certain minor-league baseball personnel.
